newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle moderately brisk $66-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle moderately brisk $66-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $66.00 per cwt in moderately active trade, unchanged from Monday, but down $1.00 from the bulk of last week's sales, feedlot sources said.

About 25,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the weekly movement near 81,500, which included 17,800 formulated and 1,200 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week.
About 26,500 head sold in Kansas, which brought the week to date movement near 30,500, including 3,400 or about 11 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle.
Sales in Kansas continued to be resisted by cattle owners anticipating strength from a turnaround in beef prices, the feedlot sources said.
Bids at $66.00 were passed by some owners asking mostly $67.00, they said.

Several feedlot sources also said they expected fed cattle prices to be underpinned by ideas packers were short bought and needed live inventory, which may explain moderately active buying so early in the week.
However, weakness in beef prices, despite increased boxed beef movement, overshadowed the market, they said.
Beef prices on Tuesday were quoted down $0.07 to $0.46 per cwt, with 434 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
